content.value_statement: Advertising platforms can claim the same sale or use incompatible attribution settings. This skill reconciles claims against verified orders and exposes double-counting.
actual_capabilities: Matches platform-reported conversions to GA4 or ecommerce order IDs.
Labels platform claims as matched, double-counted, or unmatched.
Normalizes attribution windows and currencies before comparison.
Compares credit allocation across at least two attribution models.
Calculates holdout lift when test and control exports are available.
Produces a reconciliation workbook and handoff summary.
limitations: Requires a GA4 or ecommerce order-ID export as the truth set.
Cannot infer incrementality without a valid geo or holdout test.
Does not calculate ROAS, CPA, ROI, or earned media value.
Uses timestamp and value matching only when order IDs are unavailable.

use_cases.title: Audit Cross-Platform Claims
use_cases.description: Find orders claimed by both Meta and Google, then report verified and unmatched conversions.

use_cases.title: Build Monthly Reconciliation
use_cases.description: Create a recurring workbook with normalized windows, currencies, de-duplicated counts, and unresolved mismatches.

use_cases.title: Compare Holdout Results
use_cases.description: Measure test-region lift against control data and compare incremental orders with last-click claims.

prompt_templates.title: Find Double-Counted Orders
prompt_templates.prompt: Reconcile these Meta and Google conversion exports against my GA4 order-ID export. Label every claim as matched, double-counted, or unmatched.

prompt_templates.title: Normalize Monthly Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a monthly reconciliation for [period]. Normalize all platforms to [window] and [currency], then show de-duplicated conversions by platform.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Attribution Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Reconcile these exports, then compare last-click with [linear or position-based] attribution. Explain credit shifts without changing the verified order total.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Incrementality
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these test and control exports to calculate holdout lift. Compare incremental orders with last-click claims and document assumptions and unresolved data gaps.

output_examples.input: GA4 lists 120 orders. Meta claims 82 and Google claims 71, with 24 shared order IDs.
output: Platform claims without verified orders: review required
The verified order total remains the reconciliation baseline.

output_examples.input: Meta uses seven-day click attribution, while Google uses thirty-day attribution and a different currency.
output_examples.output: The workbook aligns both exports to the selected common window and currency before matching claims to verified orders.

output_examples.input: A two-week geo holdout includes test and control order exports plus platform spend.
output_examples.output: The incrementality section reports test-versus-control lift, compares it with last-click credit, and states experiment assumptions.

best_practices: Provide complete order IDs, timestamps, values, currencies, and platform attribution windows.
Choose the common attribution window and reporting currency before matching records.
Review unmatched claims and save results only after confirming the reconciliation.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a platform-reported conversion count as the truth set.
Do not compare unnormalized windows or currencies.
Do not infer incrementality from attribution data without a control group.

faq.question: What data is required?
faq.answer: Provide a GA4 or ecommerce order-ID export and each platform conversion export. Include attribution windows and currencies.

faq.question: Can it reconcile Meta and Google together?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies shared order claims and counts each verified order once in the truth set.

faq.question: What happens when order IDs are missing?
faq.answer: The skill can match timestamps and values as a fallback, but those matches require careful review.

faq.question: Does it calculate ROAS or CPA?
faq.answer: No. It prepares verified conversion counts for a separate ROI calculation workflow.

faq.question: Can it measure incrementality?
faq.answer: Yes, when valid test and control exports exist. Otherwise, it marks incrementality as unavailable.

faq.question: Does it access advertising accounts directly?
faq.answer: No direct access is required. The documented workflow uses user-provided exports, with connectors described as optional.
